red-autumn-calville.heading: 58. CALVILLE ROUGE D'AUTOMNE.--Knoop.
red-autumn-calville.flavour: Flesh, white, tinged with red under the skin, and very much so on the side which is exposed to the sun; it is tender, delicate, and juicy, with a pleasant, vinous, and violet scented flavor.
red-autumn-calville.quality: A culinary apple of inferior quality in this country, but highly esteemed on the Continent, both as a culinary and a dessert fruit.
red-autumn-calville.storage: It is in season during October and November.
red-autumn-calville.climate: To have the fruit in perfection it ought to be grown on the paradise stock as an open dwarf, in a fine sandy loam
red-autumn-calville.note: Synonyms include Red Autumn Calville and Rothe Herbstcalville.

coccagee.heading: 73. COCCAGEE.--Hort.
coccagee.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, soft, sharply acid, and austere.
coccagee.quality: One of the oldest and best cider apples.
coccagee.note: Irish origin, brought to Minehead, Somerset c.1727 (Langley). Cider 'of the color of sherry' with 'a more vinous taste than any cyder I ever drank'. Rich flavour when baked.

styre.heading: 128. FOREST STYRE.--Knight.
styre.quality: a fine old Gloucestershire cider apple
styre.climate: extensively cultivated on the thin limestone soils of the Forest of Dean
styre.note: Synonyms Stire, Forest Styre. Says only 'Flesh, firm'; the cider is 'strong bodied, rich, and highly flavored'.

woodcock.heading: 394. WOODCOCK.--Evelyn.
woodcock.quality: one of the oldest cider apples, and is highly commended by the writers of the seventeenth century
woodcock.note: No taste words; Knight thought it had long ceased to deserve planting.
